purpose: Map what a user can SEE to where it lives in the code. A bug report says 'the notes box on a client record is broken'; this file turns that into a file and a line range instead of a 37,000-line guess.
how_to_use: Match the report's wording against `says` (the words an owner actually uses) or `surface`.
Open `file`. If `lines` is present, START THERE — for components/BeeHub.jsx that is the difference between a region and a haystack.
`routes` and `tables` are where to look next when the UI is fine but the data is wrong.
An entry is a STARTING POINT, not a conclusion. It says where to begin reading, not what is broken.

fields.surface: what the user sees, named the way a user would name it
fields.nav: which nav destination it lives under
fields.symbol: the top-level declaration in that file (verified by the guard)
fields.exported: default | named | internal — how `symbol` is declared (verified)
fields.anchor: optional literal source string that narrows to a sub-region inside `symbol` (verified unique)
fields.lines: DERIVED, never hand-written. Run `node scripts/screen-map-sync.mjs` after moving code.
fields.routes: API routes this surface calls, as 'METHOD /api/path' (verified to exist and export that method)
fields.tables: Supabase tables the surface reads or writes, via those routes (verified to be queried somewhere)
fields.says: how a non-technical person refers to this surface
fields.note: optional caveat worth knowing before you start reading

guard: lib/beta-screen-map-248.test.ts — fails when a referenced file, symbol, export kind, anchor, route, method, table, or line range no longer matches the code.
